title: Zariski inverse image injects into the etale inverse image (sheaves of sets)
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $i:Z\to X$ a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] and $F$ a sheaf of sets on the small etale site $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets]. Let $F_{\rm Zar}$ be the sheaf of sets $W\mapsto F(W\hookrightarrow X)$ on the topological space of $X$ ($W\subseteq X$ open) [lem-weil-pbc-zariski-etale-inclusion-morphism-of-sites], and let $i^{-1}_{\rm Zar}F_{\rm Zar}$ be its topological inverse image on $Z$ with unit $\eta^{\rm Zar}_W:F_{\rm Zar}(W)\to(i^{-1}_{\rm Zar}F_{\rm Zar})(i^{-1}W)$ [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image] (2), (3) with values in sets. Let $i^{-1}F$ be the etale inverse image of $F$, a sheaf of sets on $Z_{\Et}$ (the sheafification of $V\mapsto\varinjlim_{(U,\varphi)}F(U)$ over pairs of $U$ etale over $X$ and a $Z$-morphism $\varphi:V\to U\times_XZ$ [def-pc-fibre-product], as in [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-functor-sheaf-pullback-adjunction] (2) for the functor $U\mapsto U\times_XZ$, i.e. [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] with values in sets), with unit $i^*:F(U)\to(i^{-1}F)(U\times_XZ)$, and let $(i^{-1}F)_{\rm Zar}$ be the sheaf $V\mapsto(i^{-1}F)(V\hookrightarrow Z)$ on the topological space of $Z$. For $W\subseteq X$ open identify $W\times_XZ$ with the open subscheme $i^{-1}(W)$ of $Z$. Then there is exactly one morphism of sheaves of sets $\beta:i^{-1}_{\rm Zar}F_{\rm Zar}\to(i^{-1}F)_{\rm Zar}$ on $Z$ with $\beta_{i^{-1}W}(\eta^{\rm Zar}_W(s))=i^*s$ for every open $W\subseteq X$ and every $s\in F(W)$, and $\beta_V$ is injective for every open $V\subseteq Z$. In particular the canonical restriction $\Gamma(X,F)\to\Gamma(Z,i^{-1}F)$, $s\mapsto i^*s$, is the composite of $\eta^{\rm Zar}_X:\Gamma(X,F_{\rm Zar})=F(X)\to\Gamma(Z,i^{-1}_{\rm Zar}F_{\rm Zar})$ with the injective map $\beta_Z$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 09ZF (lemma-gabber-h0), proof, first paragraph ('There is a canonical (base change) map ... we obtain injectivity on stalks') and second paragraph (factorization of the restriction map)

proof.text: *Construction of $\beta$* (source: 'There is a canonical (base change) map $i^{-1}(\mathcal F|_{X_{Zar}})\to(i^{-1}_{small}\mathcal F)|_{Z_{Zar}}$'). By [lem-weil-pbc-zariski-etale-inclusion-morphism-of-sites] (3), applied on $X$ and on $Z$, $F_{\rm Zar}=\epsilon_*F$ and $(i^{-1}F)_{\rm Zar}$ are sheaves of sets on the spaces of $X$ and $Z$. For $W\subseteq X$ open, the projection $W\times_XZ\to Z$ is an open immersion [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change] with image $i^{-1}(W)$, through which it factors [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme]; with this identification $(i_{*}(i^{-1}F)_{\rm Zar})(W)=(i^{-1}F)_{\rm Zar}(i^{-1}W)=(i^{-1}F)(W\times_XZ)$, where $i_*$ is the topological direct image along the continuous map $i$ [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image] (1), a sheaf. The unit $i^*:F\to u^s i^{-1}F$ of the adjunction $u_s\dashv u^s$ for $u:X_{\Et}\to Z_{\Et}$, $U\mapsto U\times_XZ$ [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-functor-sheaf-pullback-adjunction] (2), is a morphism of presheaves on $X_{\Et}$, so $i^*(s|_{W'})=(i^*s)|_{W'\times_XZ}$ for opens $W'\subseteq W$ (the inclusion $W'\hookrightarrow W$ being a morphism of $X_{\Et}$ [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale]). Hence $\alpha_W(s)=i^*s$ defines a morphism of sheaves $\alpha:F_{\rm Zar}\to i_*(i^{-1}F)_{\rm Zar}$ on $X$. By the adjunction $i^{-1}_{\rm Zar}\dashv i_*$ of [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image] (3) with unit $\eta^{\rm Zar}$, morphisms $\beta:i^{-1}_{\rm Zar}F_{\rm Zar}\to(i^{-1}F)_{\rm Zar}$ correspond bijectively to morphisms $F_{\rm Zar}\to i_*(i^{-1}F)_{\rm Zar}$ by $\beta\mapsto i_*(\beta)\circ\eta^{\rm Zar}$ (the description of an adjunction bijection through its unit). So there is exactly one $\beta$ with $i_*(\beta)\circ\eta^{\rm Zar}=\alpha$, i.e. with $\beta_{i^{-1}W}(\eta^{\rm Zar}_W(s))=i^*s$ for all $W$ and $s\in F(W)$; this is the existence and uniqueness asserted. Since $\beta$ is a morphism of presheaves, for $z\in Z$ it induces $\beta_z:(i^{-1}_{\rm Zar}F_{\rm Zar})_z\to((i^{-1}F)_{\rm Zar})_z$ on stalks (colimits of sets over the open neighbourhoods of $z$, as in [lem-weil-pbc-sets-inverse-image-stalk]) with $\beta_z(\sigma_z)=(\beta_V(\sigma))_z$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 09ZF (lemma-gabber-h0), proof, first paragraph (first sentence)

proof.text: *The unit as a class in the presheaf inverse image.* Write $i^{-1}F=(i_pF)^\#$ with sheafification map $\theta:i_pF\to i^{-1}F$, $i_pF(V)=\varinjlim_{(U,\varphi)\in\mathcal I_V^{op}}F(U)$ over the pairs of an object $U$ of $X_{\Et}$ and a $Z$-morphism $\varphi:V\to U\times_XZ$, coprojections $\iota_{(U,\varphi)}$, and restriction along $g:V'\to V$ sending $\iota_{(U,\varphi)}(s)$ to $\iota_{(U,\varphi\circ g)}(s)$ [lem-weil-pbc-presheaf-pullback-sets-left-exact] (1), [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-functor-sheaf-pullback-adjunction] (2). The adjunction $u_s\dashv u^s$ is the composite of $u_p\dashv u^p$, whose unit at $U$ is $\iota_{(U,\mathrm{id})}$ [lem-weil-pbc-presheaf-pullback-sets-left-exact] (1), and of sheafification $\dashv$ inclusion, whose unit is $\theta$; so the composite unit is $i^*s=\theta_{U\times_XZ}(\iota_{(U,\mathrm{id})}(s))$. Consequently, for $W\subseteq X$ open, $V\subseteq i^{-1}W$ open in $Z$ with inclusion $\varphi_V:V\to W\times_XZ$ (step 1), and a $Z$-morphism $g:V'\to V$ of $Z_{\Et}$, the restriction of $i^*s$ along $\varphi_V\circ g$ is $\theta_{V'}(\iota_{(W,\varphi_V\circ g)}(s))$, since $\theta$ is a morphism of presheaves. Moreover each $\mathcal I_{V'}^{op}$ is filtered, because $X_{\Et}$ has finite limits and $U\mapsto U\times_XZ$ commutes with them [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits] (2), (3), [lem-weil-pbc-presheaf-pullback-sets-left-exact] (2).

source.place: Lemma Tag 09ZF (lemma-gabber-h0), proof, first paragraph (the description of the stalk on the right hand side as a colimit over etale neighbourhoods $(U,u)\to(X,z)$ with a section of $U\times_XZ\to Z$ near $z$); the unit as in Sites, Lemma Tag 00WX and the paragraph 'we denote $i^{-1}s$' of the same proof

proof.text: *Key step: agreement on $Z$ near $z$ gives agreement on $X$ near $i(z)$* (source: 'As \'etale morphisms are open, the image of $U\to X$ is an open neighbourhood $U_0$ of $z$ in $X$. The map $\mathcal F(U_0)\to\mathcal F(U)$ is injective by the sheaf condition for $\mathcal F$ with respect to the \'etale covering $U\to U_0$'). Let $z\in Z$, $x=i(z)$, $W\subseteq X$ an open neighbourhood of $x$, $a,b\in F(W)$, and suppose $(i^*a)|_V=(i^*b)|_V$ in $(i^{-1}F)(V)$ for some open $V\subseteq i^{-1}W$ containing $z$. We show $a|_{W_0}=b|_{W_0}$ for an open $W_0\subseteq W$ containing $x$. By step 2, $(i^*a)|_V=\theta_V(p)$ and $(i^*b)|_V=\theta_V(q)$ with $p=\iota_{(W,\varphi_V)}(a)$, $q=\iota_{(W,\varphi_V)}(b)$ in $i_pF(V)$. As $\theta_V(p)=\theta_V(q)$, there is a covering $\{g_k:V_k\to V\}$ of $Z_{\Et}$ with $p|_{V_k}=q|_{V_k}$ for all $k$ [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local]. The covering is jointly surjective [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets]: pick $k$ and $v\in V_k$ with $g_k(v)=z$. By step 2, $p|_{V_k}=\iota_{(W,\varphi_k)}(a)$ and $q|_{V_k}=\iota_{(W,\varphi_k)}(b)$, $\varphi_k=\varphi_V\circ g_k$. Since $\mathcal I_{V_k}^{op}$ is filtered (step 2), [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise] (3) gives a morphism $(U,\psi)\to(W,\varphi_k)$ of $\mathcal I_{V_k}$, i.e. an $X$-morphism $g:U\to W$ from an etale $U\to X$ with $(g\times_XZ)\circ\psi=\varphi_k$, such that $a|_U=b|_U$ (restriction along $g$). Let $u'\in U$ be the image of $\psi(v)\in U\times_XZ$; as $\psi$ is a $Z$-morphism, $\psi(v)$ lies over $z$, so $u'$ lies over $x=i(z)$. The image $W_0$ of $U\to X$ is open [lem-weil-pbc-etale-morphism-open-map], contains $x$, and lies in $W$ because $U\to X$ factors through $g$. So $U\to X$ factors as $U\xrightarrow{u_0}W_0\hookrightarrow X$ [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme]; $u_0$ is surjective by the choice of $W_0$ and etale, being a morphism between schemes etale over $X$ [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale], [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (3). Hence $\{u_0:U\to W_0\}$ is a covering of $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. The two morphisms $g$ and $(W_0\hookrightarrow W)\circ u_0$ from $U$ to $W$ become equal after composing with the open immersion $W\hookrightarrow X$, so they are equal [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-monomorphism]; therefore $(a|_{W_0})|_U=a|_U=b|_U=(b|_{W_0})|_U$ along $u_0$. The sheaf condition of $F$ for the one-member covering $\{u_0\}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets] (the first map of the equalizer diagram is injective) gives $a|_{W_0}=b|_{W_0}$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 09ZF (lemma-gabber-h0), proof, first paragraph (from 'As \'etale morphisms are open' to 'Taking the colimit over all $U$ and $U_0$')

proof.text: *$\beta_z$ is injective for every $z\in Z$* (source: 'We will show this map is injective by looking at stalks. The stalk on the left hand side at $z\in Z$ is the stalk of $\mathcal F|_{X_{Zar}}$ at $z$'; '...we obtain injectivity on stalks'). Let $x=i(z)$ and $c:(F_{\rm Zar})_x\to(i^{-1}_{\rm Zar}F_{\rm Zar})_z$ the bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-inverse-image-stalk], $c(s_x)=(\eta^{\rm Zar}_W(s))_z$. Let $\sigma,\tau$ be elements of $(i^{-1}_{\rm Zar}F_{\rm Zar})_z$. By surjectivity of $c$ and since a germ at $x$ is represented on any smaller neighbourhood (restriction to $W=W_1\cap W_2$), $\sigma=(\eta^{\rm Zar}_W(a))_z$ and $\tau=(\eta^{\rm Zar}_W(b))_z$ for one open $W\ni x$ and $a,b\in F(W)$. By step 1, $\beta_z(\sigma)=(i^*a)_z$ and $\beta_z(\tau)=(i^*b)_z$, germs in $((i^{-1}F)_{\rm Zar})_z$. Suppose they are equal. The stalk is a colimit over the directed set of open neighbourhoods of $z$, a filtered category, so by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise] (3) there is an open $V\subseteq i^{-1}W$ containing $z$ with $(i^*a)|_V=(i^*b)|_V$. By step 3 there is an open $W_0\subseteq W$ containing $x$ with $a|_{W_0}=b|_{W_0}$, so $a_x=b_x$ in $(F_{\rm Zar})_x$, and $\sigma=c(a_x)=c(b_x)=\tau$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 09ZF (lemma-gabber-h0), proof, first paragraph (second and last sentences)

proof.text: *$\beta_V$ is injective for every open $V\subseteq Z$* (source: 'injective by looking at stalks'). If $\beta_V(\sigma)=\beta_V(\tau)$ for $\sigma,\tau\in(i^{-1}_{\rm Zar}F_{\rm Zar})(V)$, then for every $z\in V$, $\beta_z(\sigma_z)=(\beta_V(\sigma))_z=(\beta_V(\tau))_z=\beta_z(\tau_z)$, so $\sigma_z=\tau_z$ by step 4; as $i^{-1}_{\rm Zar}F_{\rm Zar}$ is a sheaf of sets [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image] (3), $\sigma=\tau$ [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-sections-determined-by-germs].

source.place: Lemma Tag 09ZF (lemma-gabber-h0), proof, first paragraph (the conclusion 'We will show this map is injective by looking at stalks')

proof.text: *Factorization of the restriction on global sections* (source, second paragraph: 'It follows from this and assumption (1) that the map $\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)\to\Gamma(Z,i^{-1}_{small}\mathcal F)$ is injective'). Take $W=X$ in step 1: $i^{-1}X=Z$, $X\times_XZ=Z$, $F_{\rm Zar}(X)=F(X)=\Gamma(X,F)$ and $(i^{-1}F)_{\rm Zar}(Z)=\Gamma(Z,i^{-1}F)$; the defining identity of $\beta$ reads $\beta_Z(\eta^{\rm Zar}_X(s))=i^*s$, i.e. $s\mapsto i^*s$ is $\beta_Z\circ\eta^{\rm Zar}_X$, with $\beta_Z$ injective by step 5.

split_report.summary: Split following the first paragraph of the proof of Stacks 09ZF (and the factorization of its second paragraph) in six steps: (1) the base change map beta built by the adjunction i^{-1}_Zar -| i_* from the unit s |-> i^*s of the etale inverse image, with its uniqueness; (2) the unit written as theta of the coprojection at (U,id) of the presheaf inverse image, and filteredness of the index categories; (3) the source's key argument: equality of i^*a, i^*b near z gives, through local agreement in the sheafification, a pair (U,psi) with a|_U=b|_U and U over i(z); the image U_0 of U is open and U -> U_0 is an etale covering, so a=b on U_0; (4) injectivity of beta on stalks from the stalk bijection of the topological inverse image; (5) injectivity on sections from germs; (6) the factorization on global sections. The source's description of the right-hand stalk ('colimit over elementary etale neighbourhoods (U,u) such that U x_X Z -> Z has a section near z') is not used as a statement: step 3 works with representatives directly, which is what the source's argument needs.
